headline: Kevin Warsh, chair of the US Federal Reserve, said the rise of AI is likely to be a very bumpy ride, hitting demand first and supply later.
score_reason: Pool score kept: the head of the central bank calls AI a major economic shock, on the record, but it is a forecast.
importance_line: The head of the US central bank now calls AI a major economic shock, which matters first to people who borrow money and to firms that rely on AI spending, but it is a forecast rather than a measured result and Warsh expects a large long-run benefit.
summary: CFO Dive reports that Kevin Warsh, chair of the Federal Reserve, the US central bank, told the International Monetary Fund's annual meeting in Bangkok on Friday that AI is "probably the most consequential change" to the US and global economy "in my lifetime", but that the path there is "likely to be a very bumpy one", with AI hitting demand (as tech giants rush to buy chips, power and equipment) before supply. The article adds that borrowing by those giant cloud-computing firms has helped push the yield on the 10-year US Treasury note above 5% since mid-September, which raises borrowing costs for consumers and businesses, while Warsh still expects "a huge benefit" to the global economy in the medium term.
notes: Read on Yahoo Finance, which carries CFO Dive's own text; the original CFO Dive link was not given, so the Yahoo page is the url. Day of the speech is Friday 16 Oct 2026.
